problems.text: counterexample: triangles right -> not iso; options a=right-scalene, b=right-isosceles, c=isosceles-acute, d=obtuse-scalene

options.label: An acute isosceles triangle that is not equilateral

problems.explain: A counterexample makes the hypothesis true and the conclusion false. Check each: a right scalene triangle has a right angle and does not have two equal sides; a right isosceles triangle has a right angle and has two equal sides; an acute isosceles triangle that is not equilateral has no right angle and has two equal sides; an obtuse scalene triangle has no right angle and does not have two equal sides. Of these, only a right isosceles triangle meets the hypothesis and misses the conclusion. (A case where the hypothesis fails says nothing about the statement, whatever the conclusion does.) So a right isosceles triangle.
